comment: The boards wz's Zephyr images are built for, one row per BOARD x LINK x APP, and how far each row is WITNESSED. This file is the one place that says so; deploy/zephyr-*/boards/*.conf are the per-board settings it names, and scripts/lib/zephyr_board_table_gate.py reads both.

A claim goes no higher than the LOWEST grade its evidence reaches. DECLARED: the board is a target, nothing was built. BUILT: hosted CI builds the image for this row (Layer Qzb) and nothing has run it. QEMU: the image boots on an emulated machine and a lane reads a verdict from it (witness.lane). HARDWARE: someone ran it on the board and a ledger entry records what ran (image hash, verdict sentence, date, who).

HARDWARE needs a lab. wz publishes the image and the verdict-sentence grammar; whoever owns the board runs it and files the record. Until that record exists in the store the row stays at BUILT, however likely it looks.
A board's RMII and its 10BASE-T1S port are different rows: they are different links with different drivers, and one can be witnessed while the other is not.

rows.note: The image with the SPI probe: SCB3 opened as a master on the MikroBUS socket (through the PDL; the pinned Zephyr's own SPI binding is unusable on this chip) and the two TC6 identity registers read and logged at boot. It is built, not run. Nothing is plugged into the socket on a kit as shipped, so what this row will say on silicon is what an expansion board answers, and that is the first record a lab files.

Chip not identified, and an expansion board rather than a device of the kit: the Lite user guide names no 10BASE-T1S part (its one Ethernet is the DP83825I on RMII), and its MikroBUS socket, where the board plugs in, is not populated by default. What exists: the TC6 protocol crate (wz-oa-tc6) and its SPI seam, host-tested; the SCB master's rules (wz-spi-scb), host-tested; the master itself and the identity probe, built (the row above). What does not: a chip crate, which waits for the chip's name, and the probe is how a lab learns it.
